newsitem.title: CHINA: No amnesty for S.Korea's Chun, Roh -- rights group.
newsitem.headline: No amnesty for S.Korea's Chun, Roh -- rights group.

text.p: A human rights group on Monday condemned alleged moves afoot in South Korea to win an amnesty for former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, now serving lengthy jail terms for mutiny, treason and corruption.

The Asian Human Rights Commission said in a statement it "strongly condemns this move to grant amnesty to Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo and considers it a setback to democracy and human rights in South Korea as well as Asia in general".

"It is in the interest of human rights and democracy in Korea to stop the unprincipled attempt to grant amnesty to these two convicted criminals who have harmed the people of South Korea and their democracy," the Hong Kong-based group said.
The group said the campaign to free Chun and Roh was led by opponents of democracy and supporters of former repressive regimes, and said South Koreans were concerned about it.

"They fear that the present government may misuse its presidential power to grant amnesties to the two former presidents in order to build a political alliance between the present president, Kim Young-sam, and the country's anti-democracy forces," it said.
The group said the action might lead to a strengthening of the forces that backed the repressive practices of the previous regimes in South Korea.

A South Korean newspaper recently reported that Kim might grant an amnesty to Chun and Roh, convicted in April, to boost his party's chances at the polls this December. The paper said Kim's aides were considering August 15, Liberation Day, as the time to announce the amnesty.
Chun was sentenced to life in prison and Roh to 17 years on charges of mutiny, treason and corruption during their rule.
